chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Turning (in orthodoxy) to Allah, not associating (anything) with Him' and I said: What is orthodoxy? He said: It is innateness.

key_terms.الْحَنِفِيَّةُ: Orthodoxy, the state of being Hanif
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Innate nature, natural disposition towards God
key_terms.حُنَفَاءَ: Orthodox monotheists, those turning purely to God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Hanifiyyah in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the term 'Hanifiyyah' from Quran 22:31 by equating it with 'Fitrah', the innate monotheistic disposition inherent in every human soul. This definition underscores the Shia theological view that true orthodoxy is not merely a cultural or legal adherence, but a return to the primordial state of recognizing God's oneness, aligning with the concept of *Tawhid* as a natural instinct rather than an acquired belief.
